clue.text: Collector of cuttings from Spy and Punch?

blocks.note: a grass is slang for an informer, someone who spies and tells
to box someone is to punch them

explanation.surface: A cartoonist's scrapbook of press cuttings taken from Spy and Punch, two old satirical magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: Spy and Punch look like magazine titles and 'cuttings' like newspaper clippings; really the cuttings are lawn clippings. A GRASS is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: On a lawnmower the box catching mown clippings is called by this name, so it literally gathers lawn trimmings.

clue.text: Gujarati leader and two successors

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written
the two letters that follow G in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A political leader from Gujarat followed by the two people who succeeded him.
explanation.walkthrough: The successors are not people but the letters after G in the alphabet. Mahatma GANDHI was born in Gujarat, so 'Gujarati leader' also reads as a definition of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohandas Gandhi, the Indian independence figure, came from Porbandar in Gujarat state, making him a celebrated leader from that region.

clue.text: Draw a rotten apple

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so its letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist told to sketch a rotten apple for a still life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' reads as a verb about sketching, but it is the noun meaning attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is something that attracts people, and appeal is the quality of attracting interest, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Regimen ruling out stuffing; blocking fries and sweet drinks

indicators.note: excluding the filling of a word leaves just its two outside letters
to block something is to sit in its way, inside it

blocks.note: sautées is a spelling of sautés, fries quickly in a pan
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dieting regime that bans stuffing and blocks chips and sugary drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In the dieting picture 'fries' is a noun meaning chips, but it is the cooking verb, here in its less common spelling with a double E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from Bordeaux, and the plural form here names several glasses or bottles of it.

clue.text: Politicians, without hint of shame, engaged in out-and-out exaggeration

indicators.note: without means lacking, so one letter is taken away
a hint is just a first trace, so only the opening letter is the one removed
to be engaged in something is to be involved within it

blocks.note: overt means open, undisguised, out-and-out
statesmen are political leaders
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Shameless politicians indulging in blatant exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hint of shame' takes just one letter away, and only one of the two S's in the politicians goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exaggeration and overstatement both mean presenting something as larger or more important than it really is; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Shakespeare’s ghost, clutching battered hat, starts to irritate chess club

indicators.note: something battered has been knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
to clutch is to grip, so one piece holds another
the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: the ghost in Hamlet is the dead King Hamlet, the prince's father, i.e. old Hamlet
the letters of the word rearranged
the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A ghost from Shakespeare in a crumpled hat haunts a chess club, annoying its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chess club' reads as one thing, but chess supplies a first letter and club alone is the definition. OLDHAM ATHLETIC is an English football club from Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldham Athletic is a professional English football team, known as the Latics, so it is a sports club.

clue.text: Third part of Gormenghast missing from book shelf

indicators.note: the third part of a word here is its third letter
something missing from a whole has been taken out of it

blocks.note: an account book
the third letter of the word

explanation.surface: The third volume of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast trilogy is missing from a bookshelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book shelf' reads as one item; book gives LEDGER and shelf is the definition. Gormenghast trilogy talk tempts you towards a volume title, but only its third letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow horizontal surface projecting from a wall, which is just what a shelf is.

clue.text: Teacher’s sexy selfie

blocks.note: a head is a head teacher; with the 's it is 'head is' or 'head's'
hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: A scandal: a teacher's racy self-portrait photo.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the head is the principal of a school, so 'teacher' points to HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A selfie is often a photo of one's face, and a headshot is a portrait photograph of the face, so the definition is loose.

clue.text: Moment day-tripper lost heart to bus driver

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the middle letter is taken
what is lost is no longer there, so a letter goes

blocks.note: a mo is a short moment, as in 'half a mo'
a day-tripper is a kind of tourist
the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: The moment a day-tripper fell for the bus driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bus driver' reads as one phrase and 'lost heart to' as falling in love; in fact bus supplies its central U, which the tourist loses, and 'driver' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Any person who drives a car is a motorist, so a driver on the road is this.

clue.text: Jovial brother to write back and create harmony

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: to pen is to write
to tune is to bring into harmony

explanation.surface: A cheerful brother writes back to patch up a family quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jovial' looks like 'cheerful', but here it means 'of Jove' (Jupiter): the Roman sea god was Jupiter's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth Neptune, god of the sea, was a sibling of Jupiter, also called Jove, so he is Jove's brother.

clue.text: Ancient mariner might use this to cure 5?

definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: an experienced veteran sailor
second meaning: 5 is read as two words, an aged ham, and aged sodium chloride would preserve it

explanation.surface: Wondering what an ancient sailor uses to heal some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the first word of 5-across read as OLD HAM; 'cure' is salting meat, not healing.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt is a seasoned sailor; an old one is a veteran seafarer, and literal aged salt preserves meat.

clue.text: Conductor interacting with field, releasing current, may result in electrical discharge

indicators.note: to release something is to let it go, so a letter departs
things interacting mix together, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A physics description: a conductor in a magnetic field producing a spark.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical vocabulary is all surface except 'current', which gives I; the answer is a weather term.
explanation.definitionFit: An occluded front, where a cold front overtakes a warm one, often brings thunderstorms and so lightning.

clue.text: Project Endless Bliss

indicators.note: something with no end has had its final letter cut off

blocks.note: a state of bliss

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the name of a scheme, Project Endless Bliss; 'Project' is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to throw or hurl it forward, and to heave is to throw something heavy with effort.

clue.text: Wild crocuses adorn son and heir

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so the letters run free into a new order
to adorn is to decorate around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Wild spring flowers are used to decorate a son and heir's celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son and heir' reads as one stock phrase, but son is the wordplay and heir alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who inherits a title or position, the one who comes after the current holder.

clue.text: Unhealthy popular suspicion surrounded old burial ground

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed up, so its letters are broken and remixed
to surround is to enclose, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: what is in is fashionable, popular
sus is British slang for suspicion
the letters of the word rearranged
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A grim, widespread suspicion surrounding an ancient cemetery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burial ground' reads as cemetery, but 'ground' is the anagram signal; the shuffled word follows O inside SUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Insalubrious means not conducive to health, the negative of salubrious, so it plainly matches unhealthy.

clue.text: Put out unwrapped gift – tactful to dispense with show

indicators.note: with its wrapping taken off, a word loses its outer letters
to dispense with is to do without, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: a present is a gift
taken as written
an act is a show or performance

explanation.surface: Annoyed at an unwrapped gift, but tactfully not showing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like a verb (to set out the gift), but it is the adjective meaning annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put out is offended and annoyed, and resentful describes feeling bitter indignation at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Both leads quit Top Gun musical comedy

indicators.note: the leads are the front letters, and each of the two words loses its own

blocks.note: taken as written
a Beretta is an Italian make of gun

explanation.surface: Both stars walk out of a stage musical version of Top Gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top Gun' reads as the film title, but it is two words: TOP and a gun brand, each losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera with spoken dialogue and comic plots, a forerunner of the musical.

clue.text: To a large extent artificer, am I still artisan?

indicators.note: only a large part of the words is used, so the answer lies within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word through most of the last

explanation.surface: A craftsman asking whether, broadly, he still counts as an artisan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'artificer' through 'am I' into 'still', which loses its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramist is a potter or maker of ceramics, a skilled craftsperson working by hand, which is an artisan.

clue.text: Official statement showing how to open security door

definitions.note: a cryptic instruction rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: an announcement issued to journalists
second meaning: push the button marked for unlocking

explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction, the phrase says to push the button that unlocks the door.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisations issue a press release as their formal announcement to the media, an official statement of news.

clue.text: Bird’s eggs served up on time in Paris and Rome

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ova are eggs
Central European Time, the time zone of France and Italy

explanation.surface: Eggs served at breakfast on schedule in two European capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in Bird's means 'bird is'. 'Time in Paris' tempts a French word for time, but it is a time zone abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned bill, emblem of the RSPB.

clue.text: Clergyman ensconced in motorcycle rickshaw

indicators.note: to be ensconced is to be settled snugly inside, so the answer sits within the words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A priest sitting comfortably in a motorised rickshaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'motorcycle' and the start of 'rickshaw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, such as a priest or minister, so it is a clergyman.

clue.text: Wreckage of boats caught by rocks – subject of old English ballad

indicators.note: a wreck is broken up, so the letters are scattered and reformed
something caught is held inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the letters of the word rearranged
a reef is a ridge of rocks in the sea

explanation.surface: A shipwreck on the rocks, the kind of event old English ballads sing about.
explanation.walkthrough: The shipwreck surface suggests a sea shanty; the ballad is actually 'The Roast Beef of Old England', an 18th-century patriotic song by Henry Fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielding's song 'The Roast Beef of Old England' celebrates the dish as a symbol of English virtue.

clue.text: This particular thank you letter

blocks.note: the definite article points to one particular thing
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Talking about one specific thank-you note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thank you letter' reads as a note of thanks; the letter is a Greek one.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet, written as θ, so it is a letter.

clue.text: New Amsterdam, for instance

blocks.note: first meaning: original, not seen before
second meaning: Ian McEwan's Booker-winning book Amsterdam is an example

explanation.walkthrough: New Amsterdam was the old name for New York, but the comma splits it into an adjective and an example of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel as an adjective means new and unusual; as a noun it is a long prose fiction such as McEwan's Amsterdam.

clue.text: Nuclear missile in possession of 9

definitions.note: a cryptic description, meaning what 9-across holds

blocks.note: first meaning: the submarine-launched ballistic missile system carried by the Royal Navy
second meaning: the three-pronged spear the sea god carries

explanation.surface: A nuclear weapon in the hands of a sea power.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 9-across, the Roman sea god, whose emblem is a three-pronged spear.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the name of Britain's submarine-based nuclear missile, and also the three-pronged spear held by Neptune.

clue.text: Soldier on holiday with cake decorator

blocks.note: someone off is away from work
someone who ices a cake

explanation.surface: A soldier on leave taking up cake decorating.
explanation.walkthrough: ICER is a made-up agent noun, one who applies icing.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer is a commissioned member of the armed forces, so a soldier of rank; the definition is loose.

clue.text: Comedian perhaps from America abandons usual material

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so these letters are dropped

blocks.note: a comedian is an example of a stage act
taken as written
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: An American comic ditches the usual routine for fresh material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a comedian's jokes, but it is the adjective meaning real or relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Material can mean physical or real rather than imaginary, and actual means existing in fact, so the adjectives match.
